source.author: cic
source.text: Tum Crassus quorsum igitur haec spectat inquit tam longa et tam alte repetita oratio?
source.text_original: Tum Crassus 'quorsum igitur haec spectat' inquit 'tam longa et tam alte repetita oratio?
source.text_english: Then Crassus said, To what end, then, does this speech tend, so long and so far-ranging in its retrospect?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quorsum, inquies, haec tam longo repetita principio? uidelicet ne quicquam fidei tuae deesse putes, quia Hierosolymam non uidisti, nec nos idcirco meliores aestimes, quod huius loci habitaculo fruimur, sed siue hic siue alibi aequalem te pro operibus tuis apud deum nostrum habere mercedem.
reuse.text_original: 'Quorsum', inquies, 'haec tam longo repetita principio?' uidelicet ne quicquam fidei tuae deesse putes, quia Hierosolymam non uidisti, nec nos idcirco meliores aestimes, quod huius loci habitaculo fruimur, sed siue hic siue alibi aequalem te pro operibus tuis apud deum nostrum habere mercedem.
reuse.text_english: You will say, To what end is this matter, repeated from so long a beginning? Namely, so that you may not think that anything is lacking to your faith because you have not seen Hierosolymam, nor for that reason esteem us better because we enjoy the dwelling place of this region, but rather that whether here or elsewhere you may have an equal reward with God according to your works.
